title: SolvedOnce Fix Packet
description: A model-authored, privacy-scrubbed, executable record of a newly solved problem in public software. Draft v0.3. Packets are untrusted input: the schema is strict and rejects unknown fields.

packet_id.description: Random identifier generated client-side. Must not encode user or account identity.

note.description: Optional free text. Not used for verification. Scanned like every other text field (stage E).

scope.description: Only problems in software other people also use are eligible. Bugs in private code are out of scope.

target.description: The public component the problem lives in.

license.description: SPDX identifier of the target's license. A patch derived from the target's code inherits it; it decides whether the patch may go into the public archive under its default license.

symptom.description: What the user observed. Error text must be scrubbed.

root_cause.description: Why it happens, as established during the session.

error_signature.description: Normalized error raised by the target itself, used for retrieval and deduplication. Null for silent wrong-output bugs; retrieval then falls back to target, version range and symptom similarity.

novelty_check.description: Evidence that the problem was new to the model and not already known (stage A). Self-reported here; re-checked by the provider in stage G.

model_solved_unaided.description: If the model solved it from existing knowledge, no packet is generated.

failed_attempts.description: Recorded from the session trace, not from the model's introspection: approaches the agent actually tried that did not fix the failing test.

reproduction.description: Minimal, self-contained, rewritten by the model. Never a copy of the user's code. Evidence must come from running exactly this reproduction.

dependencies.description: Exact pinned versions. The sandbox pre-fetches these from a mirror; the test itself runs without network.

patch.description: Unified diff against the target, if the fix is a code change.

evidence.description: Produced client-side by running the minimal reproduction above (not the user's original code), then re-verified independently in the provider sandbox (stage G).

authored_by.description: Humans do not hand-write packet content. This raises the bar for injection but does not remove it; stages E, G and H still apply.

session_ref.description: Opaque reference to the agent session in the provider's own records. The provider checks the packet against that record (stage G); a packet with no matching session is rejected. Must not encode user identity.

allow_public_release.description: May the verified packet be published openly (stage K)?

allow_upstream_report.description: May an issue/PR be opened upstream (stage L)?

attribution.description: Public name or handle to credit, or null to stay anonymous.
